original_question: Construct maximal signed graphs whose smallest adjacency eigenvalue is at least -3.
target_in_paper: Problem 3.16 in Section 3.4 ("The smallest eigenvalue of signed graphs"): "Construct maximal signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −3." The paragraph immediately before it explains that this is the signed-graph analogue of constructing "(−3)-maximal" graphs. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact construction task, the correct object class (signed graphs), and the correct spectral threshold (at least −3). It also correctly speaks about the adjacency eigenvalue, which matches the paper’s standing convention that the paper is working primarily with the adjacency matrix A(Γ) and its eigenvalues λ1(Γ) ≥ ··· ≥ λn(Γ). ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s eigenvalues here are adjacency eigenvalues: for a signed graph Γ = (G, σ), A(Γ) is the symmetric {0, +1, −1}-matrix with entries given by the edge signs, and the smallest eigenvalue means λn(Γ), the least eigenvalue of A(Γ). ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Connectedness is implicit but essential. In the nearby paragraph, the paper defines "(−3)-maximal" graphs as connected graphs, so a stand-alone formulation should say "connected signed graphs." ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

"Maximal" needs the paper’s exact meaning, not an informal one: Γ should satisfy λmin(A(Γ)) ≥ −3, but every proper connected supergraph should have smallest eigenvalue < −3. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The supergraph condition should be kept exactly as in the paper. The nearby text says "proper connected supergraph" and does not specialize this to "induced," "spanning," or "edge-added only," so a faithful rewrite should not sharpen it further. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The paper does not state the problem as a classification up to isomorphism or switching isomorphism. Since those notions are defined in the introduction but not invoked in Problem 3.16, a paper-faithful rewrite should not add them. This is an inference from the paper’s terminology and wording. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: Construct connected signed graphs Γ = (G, σ) that are maximal with respect to the property λmin(A(Γ)) ≥ −3; equivalently, construct connected signed graphs Γ whose signed adjacency matrix A(Γ) has smallest eigenvalue at least −3 and such that every proper connected supergraph H of Γ satisfies λmin(A(H)) < −3. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Construct connected signed graphs that are "(−3)-maximal" in the sense of the paragraph immediately preceding Problem 3.16. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
justification: The draft is very close to the exact official problem, but it is not fully stand-alone because the paper uses a specialized meaning of "maximal" that is supplied only in the immediately preceding paragraph, and that definition includes connectedness. The introduction also fixes that eigenvalues are those of the signed adjacency matrix A(Γ), so the refined version should make that explicit. I did not broaden the task to integrability, Hoffman graphs, switching classes, or any other neighboring topic, because the exact target here is Problem 3.16 itself. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
